chunks: Whoever arrives for hajj, performs tawaf around the House, and prays two rak'ahs, Allah writes for him seventy thousand good deeds, erases from him seventy thousand evil deeds, raises for him seventy thousand degrees, grants him intercession regarding seventy thousand needs, and writes for him the emancipation of seventy thousand slaves, the value of each slave being ten thousand dirhams.

key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah
key_terms.حَاجَةٍ: a need for which intercession is granted
key_terms.حَاجًّا: one who comes as a pilgrim for hajj
key_terms.حَسَنَةٍ: a good deed recorded as reward
key_terms.دَرَجَةٍ: a rank or degree of elevation
key_terms.رَقَبَةٍ: a slave, in the sense of one emancipated
key_terms.سَيِّئَةٍ: a sin or evil deed that is erased

ai.seo_question: What reward is mentioned for a pilgrim who performs tawaf of the House and prays two rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the immense reward for the pilgrim who performs tawaf of the Ka'bah and then prays two rak'ahs. It emphasizes the forgiveness of sins, elevation in rank, fulfillment through intercession, and vast reward equivalent to freeing many slaves.
